claims.claim: Reviewers describe experiencing random, severe frame-rate drops and performance stutter.

citations.review_text: I've made two attempts to play this and I quit in disgust everytime. I could go on about EA and whatnot, but I'll just say that this game takes the worst elements of AAA story-game slop and soul-slop and melds them into an extra impressive suck sandwich. Imagine a game where the FPS reduces to 3FPS for about ten seconds randombly and imaging what it's like to combine that with the loss-on-death and dodge-focused gameplay of souls and you'll understand why I quit this.

While the game itself seems good. Do NOT buy it on PC (or anywhere for that matter as leaving a game in this state shouldn't be rewarded with sales).

I've had to do so much troubleshooting just to get this thing to run at a playable, smooth framerate that I felt like I was transported back to 2004 trying to get Doom 3 to run on an old Voodoo II. It is absolutely unacceptable that this is such an intractable issue even SEVEN years after this game's launch!

I really have been enjoying the game play and the story is quite nice, but the optimization for this game is terrible. I have PC specs wayyyyyy above what is necessary to run this game, supposedly. But the game freezes and lags all the time, I understand that it's a big game with big demands but to be glitching mid fight is ridiculous. I feel like 25% of the time I'm fighting the game's code rather than the enemies in the game. 

BTW I lowered all the settings to lowest resolution turned off all the fancy lighting settings and set my FPS to cap at 45 fps. And all that still isn't enough to keep the game stable to just beat a single guy.

I really do enjoy this game for what it is without the lag and I'm a huge Star War's fan having seen almost all movies and shows. But I can't justify the performance this game has been giving me, triple A studios making crap optimizations for games is messed up and don't deserve your money.

If you really want to play this game and enjoy it, play it on console.

Truly a sad day to be a star wars fan, I will finish the game, I'm determined of that. But you won't be catching me playing Jedi Survivor any time soon.

Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order delivers an enjoyable experience with satisfying combat and challenging boss fights but unfortunately, its technical shortcomings hold it back from being a truly polished game.

The combat is one of the game's strongest aspects. The Souls-like mechanics are a great addition, making fights against bosses particularly engaging and rewarding. The game can be quite challenging, depending on your chosen difficulty. I played on Jedi Knight, the second difficulty level, and found the combat challenging without being overly punishing. The stormtroopers also seem to have surprisingly good aim compared to their movie counterparts!

Unfortunately, the technical performance is a major drawback. While the lighting looks great, I encountered several graphical glitches, including flickering textures, randomly shaking shadows, and enemies being launched into the air after being killed. I also experienced significant FPS drops of around 25–40 FPS at times, as well as occasional crashes. On top of that, enemies would sometimes glitch into walls or underneath bridges, making them impossible to kill. These issues significantly detract from the overall experience and make the game feel poorly optimized. What's particularly disappointing is that performance issues aren't exclusive to the PC version, as console players have also reported similar problems. This makes the game's technical shortcomings even more frustrating.

Customization is another mixed bag. I absolutely loved the variety of lightsaber customization options, which allow you to personalize your weapon to your liking. However, I found the outfit customization somewhat underwhelming. The limited selection of outfits, combined with the inability to customize Cal's appearance beyond options such as ponchos, left me wanting more variety.

Despite these shortcomings, Jedi: Fallen Order delivers a genuinely enjoyable Star Wars experience. The combat, challenging encounters, and lightsaber mech…

citations.review_text:
I saw so much praise for this game over the years that I was surprised I left it linger in my backlog for so long. I knew I had started it at one point. Why had I left it all this time? Booted it up, and slowly I began to realise that I had played more of it than I remembered. Strange, i thought, forgetting a game so entirely, but oh well! 

Then, a while later I remembered: I do not like this game.
The combat is meh, all the fun stuff like "oooh, an overhead slash" are locked behind having Force MP. Small rat monsters will be the bane of your existence, you will automatically kill any stormtrooper with a gun just by blocking even if he was six miles away and you hadn't even seen him. You can't wear a helmet! WHY! 99% of the exploration is "rewarded" by a new colour for your jumper. I mean. Damn. Who cares about that? 

It may have been the best star wars game in a while, but it was blaaaaaaaaaand.

7,5/10

Biggest negatives:
Exploration is not rewarding at all
Levels can feel like mazes
Terrible cosmetics
Map is pretty terrible
Terrible job at guiding the player
Very predictable exploration loop and predictable monsters. Just skip exploring, its a fiasco
Black lady's eyes are bulging out of their sockets (theres a mod fix)
Should have made combat more stylish

Overall, I think Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order is a fun action adventure/souls-like game and is worth buying and playing, especially when on sale. For me, this game is almost brilliant. It's full of "almost brilliant" moments that miss the mark in frustrating ways.

The combat is almost there. Sekiro style Jedi combat is an amazing idea. When the fights are good, they are incredible. But, the game is also full of things like annoying gank fights and frustrating hit boxes which are poorly calibrated. If they had stuck more to one on one duels and really refined that system, it would have been outstanding. I love tough games that force you to master the combat (like Sekiro). This could have been one of those games, but it falls short.

The world design is pretty awesome. But, then the game forces you to repeatedly backtrack through long levels with no fast travel, resulting in long stretches of boring gameplay just to retrieve a few minor rewards. There's a ton of customization, but it's really just 23 colors of the exact same kind of weird looking poncho. When most of the rewards you receive from exploration are just bland customization options, it can feel underwhelming.

The movement system is great. But, they overuse it to do way too much platforming. Some platforming is fine, but sometimes this game feels like it wants to be Tomb Raider.

Despite all of these gripes, the game is still fun. They nailed a lot of things: the art design, sound design, music and voice acting are all great. And the foundation of the game is incredible. I just wish they'd done more refinement before shipping this thing.

I haven't played the sequel yet. I really hope it fixes the issues I listed out. Because, if it did, it will be one hell of a video game.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game lacks a fast travel system, forcing players to run all the way back through previously cleared levels after completing objectives.

citations.review_text:
I was hesitant on whether to give this game a positive or a negative review at first. The essence of Star Wars is there and I really like that, but my problem is primarily with the gameplay. There is no sense of progression, the same enemies that you fight 5 mins into the game are the same ones you fight at the last 5 mins. Somehow they're still annoying to fight, they stun you a lot, and make it hard to execute combos or attacks. The abilities are nice but the focus bar runs out fast, so most of the time you're just spamming square and end up only using normal attacks that usually barely do damage. Traversing the game is horrible, slow, and exhausting. For some reason there is no fast travel. Maps are huge and when you finish your objective, you're forced to backtrack all the way back, and this literally happens throughout the whole game.

Now as for the story, I thought it was pretty good for the first 95% of it but it wasn't something that crazy. Until I got to the last 5% and [spoiler]DARTH MUTHA FUCKIN VADER APPEARED OUT OF NOWHERE[/spoiler]. That alone made me love the game way more and made it worth playing.

Overall, although the gameplay isn't great and feels stiff at times, if you love Star Wars lore, I would still recommend this game. The ending is worth it in my books.

Overall, I think Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order is a fun action adventure/souls-like game and is worth buying and playing, especially when on sale. For me, this game is almost brilliant. It's full of "almost brilliant" moments that miss the mark in frustrating ways.

There's a ton of customization, but it's really just 23 colors of the exact same kind of weird looking poncho. When most of the rewards you receive from exploration are just bland customization options, it can feel underwhelming.

The movement system is great. But, they overuse it to do way too much platforming. Some platforming is fine, but sometimes this game feels like it wants to be Tomb Raider.

Despite all of these gripes, the game is still fun. They nailed a lot of things: the art design, sound design, music and voice acting are all great. And the foundation of the game is incredible. I just wish they'd done more refinement before shipping this thing.

I haven't played the sequel yet. I really hope it fixes the issues I listed out. Because, if it did, it will be one hell of a video game.

citations.review_text:
For me this is the classic star wars experience, hack and slash - with the lightsaber. I used to play split screen on the PS1 with my neighbour back in 99-00 so this game is pure nostalgia for me. It looks great with graphics turned all the way up and seems to run flawlessly on linux - although CPU usage frequently hits 100%. -It requires the EA app to play a singleplayer game

Most of my "play time" is just me fighting with the ea login drm virus that comes with this game. There is no reason for anti-cheat or whatever this is on a single player game. claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat system as heavily focused on precise timing for parries and dodges, which can feel restrictive or awkward when facing multiple enemies simultaneously.

citations.review_text:
Tomb Raider: Star Wars Edition

+ Weaves past star wars story elements into a new story without feeling like a blatant rehash
+  Interesting exploration and investigation
+ Metroidvania letting you re-explore old areas to open up new places

- Lightsaber feels weak (can only cut through a few things)
- Combat is the "time your parry just right THEN attack" trope which I'm really sick of
- Crowd control with a lightsaber is impossible unless you spam force powers to hobble enemies
- Graphics get smudgy at times, even on "epic" setting (too much anti-aliasing or bloom or blur)

Like someone else said, they took Tomb Raider and mashed it up with Souls-like combat. Because it's Star Wars, every setting has extreme machinery or environmental hazards. So, you'll either love or hate that. But, I'm really tired of this "you must parry JUST RIGHT and THEN strike back" combat junk that the Souls-like genre has produced.

As a jedi I should be able to use a "hard" stance and just go in swinging and breaking through defenses. Instead, you're left constantly on-guard until enemies strike. Because if you don't, they'll just parry and cheap-shot you. So, you have to wait for them to attack so YOU can parry and cheap-shot them.

I was playing on STORY MODE, and still getting my rear beaten by enemies. Once you get 2+ enemies in a fight it becomes a struggle to crowd control. In other games they'll have cues to let you click a block button to insta-catch an attacker's attack and then counter. But, here, you're just trying to notice the enemy attack, you hit your block button, and hopefully you block. Then you can try to attac-.. oh, wait.. the enemy has one or two more attacks to do.. so since you stopped blocking and decided to attack they just wail on you.

Combat becomes an aggravating chore that interrupts the exploration and story.

But, even the exploration is a bit pointless. You gain xp by finding stuff, and that gives you points to unlock skills. But, stuff you find in crat…

Jedi: Survivor is one of my favorite games, so I came to Fallen Order with lowered expectations, hoping to scratch the same itch. I couldn’t finish it.

The problem is combat design. Survivor gives you real tools to handle enemies that can one-shot or stun-lock you, so a sniper behind a pack of ten isn’t a death sentence. Fallen Order’s toolkit is much thinner. Fighting five enemies at once, you’ll get animation-locked by a flamethrower clone and die without much you can do about it.

Then the respawns make it worse. Survivor deliberately puts meditation points right before bosses, so you can jump straight back in. In Fallen Order, you often respawn far back and have to clear two packs of enemies you already beat, just to die to the same thing again. It’s the kind of frustration that makes you want to throw your controller.

If you’re new to the series, you might be able to tolerate this, and I’ve heard the story is great as a prequel to Survivor. But if you’re coming from Survivor, the step back is unbearable. I uninstalled it, and I’m genuinely disappointed. Not recommended for Survivor fans.

This game fumbles the ball so hard it's baffling. The premise, a puzzle-platformer with souls/sekiro-lite elements and a flavouring of metroidvania sounds like it would be an awesome framework for a Star Wars game. Respawn, however, does not commit hard enough to any of these elements, or simply fails to implement them in a way that is fun/works well. The word of the day for Fallen Order is frustrating. The platforming and puzzles can be great, or the game can eat an input and you fall of a cliff, or miss a grab when you have to catch a ledge: frustrating. The game wants you to parry and perfect dodge, but enemies can attack simultaneously, causing you to miss a parry, stagger and eat one or more hits. Some attacks are very, very poorly telegraphed: frustrating. The game wants you to return to old areas and use your new abilities to explore them, but demands you spend 5-10 minutes hoofing it through a map you've cleared before for a single chest, then go all the way back without shortcuts: frustrating.

Somewhere buried deep beneath the confusing and annoying execution of Fallen Order sits one of the greatest SW games in recent history, but this sadly isn't it.

combat is so clunky, half the time when fighting any enemy, trying to block or dodge is terrible as most enemys are programmed to do a  special attack when they light up red. just trying to block an attack wont work especially when fighting purge troopers or haxion brood bounty hunters

Loved the movie-like cinematics and the story, even though I'm not very familiar with the franchise. Fighting  feels a bit clunky sometimes (parry is a bit inconsistent for example) and some of the puzzles may cause you to scream into a pillow, but that's all good for a souls-lite.

I got this game for the huge may 4th discount and man was it worth every dollar spent. Combat and gameplay, while at times can be janky, is also very satisfying and fun to learn. Story is also great, with some of the best star wars we've gotten since Disney took over in my opinion. Definitely worth it playing, especially if its on sale (Which is fairly often).

Good, but 7-8/10 good, not more for me. I played on 3rd difficulty level. Decent gameplay, good combat system though there is a tiny bit of jankiness in it compared to top tier games with soulslike combat. Maps are so complex that it's both an achievement to praise and a liability, going back to some missing chests combined with no convenient teleport system can be pain in the ass. Game is kinda short but not too short.

Surprisingly good for game made by EA.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that navigating the maps and backtracking without a fast travel system makes collecting items and completing areas tedious and confusing.

citations.review_text:
Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order is proof of how good a child of Dark Souls and the Star Wars IP can be, paired with a few Metroidvania elements that, in my opinion, work well. Cal and BD-1 are fresh, untainted characters who are given a great story. The planets you visit are all visually appealing and offer different flora, fauna, power-ups, and, of course, boss enemies. The variety of enemies is not outstanding, but certainly solid and the big creatures are fascinating. There is also a great bestiary and a good skill tree. Personally, I'm not the biggest fan of most of the human NPCs, but Greez carries. The technical state is solid as well.

The only major points of criticism for me were:
- passing through narrow passages too often
- loot consisting mostly of skins and therefore not being very motivating
- map navigation (for 100% completion)

I don't like souls-likes. Combat is often far too challenging, even with rank and file enemies. Or maybe I just suck. Regardless, add a Story-mode difficulty, a lot of sci-fi and Star Wars and all of a sudden I'm interested. STAR WARS Jedi: Fallen Order introduces plenty of new, interesting characters into the universe we all love. The voice acting and motion captured cutscenes are great. The story is captivating. It's a wonderful game.

There are a few puzzles and locations that are a bit frustrating. Backtracking is fine. The glaring problem is the lack of a fast travel system on planets.

Took me 50 hours in Jedi Master (Second hardest) difficulty to 100% this game, and I feel it shouldn't have taken this long, had the devs included fast travel points (backtracking 80% of a planet just to scan a bird's feather was frustrating). But I hear they have included them in the sequel so I will not complain. And I mustn't complain about this game at all, because it is a masterpiece. Having to constantly parry to reduce enemy stamina, landing a strike and repeating the process until the enemy is dead, has never felt more satisfying to me. Having watched most of the Star Wars content on the screen out there, the characters, their motivations, story plot points and twists were truely exciting to watch and participate in as a young Jedi survivor. Sure, its yet another MacGuffin pursuit in the company of misfits in an iconic-looking spaceship jumping from planets to planets like many other Star Wars stories. But like Mr. Lucas once said, "It's like poetry. It rhymes." And I loved every rhythm, every meter, every verse and rhyme of this Limerick.

I’ve already played this game twice on Xbox, putting around 90 hours into it, before buying it again on Steam. Replaying it for a third time now, I still love this game and Star Wars as a whole.

The Story is by far my favourite part of the game. The Second Sister is my favourite villain out of these games (apart from Darth Vader) I love her design and presence whenever she’s on screen and [spoiler]the connection between her and Cere is executed beautifully and is still the best part of this game[/spoiler]

I also liked all of the main characters. Cere, Greez, BD-1 and [spoiler]Merrin[/spoiler]. Greez is my favourite out of them with Cere coming at a close second.

The Graphics in this game are jaw dropping. Everything looks absolutely amazing and all of the planets have a very unique feel to them. I absolutely love how Zeffo and Ilum looks.

The Gameplay is great. The single bladed and double bladed lightsabers are so much fun to use in these games and the force powers you unlock during the story is also incredibly fun to use. Though it's a bit of a shame there's no dismemberment it makes me feel like I have a sequel lightsaber.

One of the few complaints I have is the backtracking in this game. It got annoying to constantly go back and forth between the different planets because of the lack of fast travel, which also made getting the collectibles a bit more annoying but it wasn't a major issue I had. Screw those Zeffo Trials though, I always get stuck on them. 

PC Performance is also something to take note of. I experienced stutters while traversing through the planets and even within Cutscenes when travelling to different planets. I didn’t find it to be that big of a deal though and it mostly only happened to me when huge chunks of the map were being loaded in.

Overall though I think Jedi: Fallen Order is an absolutely amazing game and I thoroughly enjoyed each one of my playthroughs on Xbox and Steam. If you’re a fan of Star Wars. This game is an absolute blas…

incredible game , good story and probably the best star wars game out there right now , total 9/10 game, the only downside  being there their is no fast travel , so it gets frustating with the puzzles, the best beginner friendly game for people who are new or wants to try out souls game , this could be the starting point .

Good, but 7-8/10 good, not more for me. I played on 3rd difficulty level. Decent gameplay, good combat system though there is a tiny bit of jankiness in it compared to top tier games with soulslike combat. Maps are so complex that it's both an achievement to praise and a liability, going back to some missing chests combined with no convenient teleport system can be pain in the ass. Game is kinda short but not too short.

Surprisingly good for game made by EA.
